nodes.content: Develop visual question answering that responds to causally relevant image changes while remaining invariant to distractors under compositional shift.
requirements: Answer both original and answer-changing counterfactual images correctly on at least 80% of fixed-question pairs.
Limit answer changes under irrelevant visual edits to 5% on unseen object–attribute combinations.

nodes.content: Train region-grounded VQA with question-conditioned masks, counterfactual answer supervision, distractor-invariance loss, and object–attribute recombination augmentation.
Can question-conditioned masks preserve relation-critical regions while excluding edited distractors on unseen object–attribute combinations?
On unseen combinations, counterfactual-supervised masks achieve ≥90% relation-region recall and ≤5% edited-distractor coverage.
Measure relation-region recall and edited-distractor coverage for counterfactual-supervised masks on CompoEdit-1’s held-out object–attribute pairs.
On CompoEdit-1 held-out pairs, masks reached 92% relation-region recall but covered 13% of edited distractors, exceeding 5%.
Retain counterfactual-supervised masks but add edited-distractor exclusion loss, since 13% coverage exceeds the 5% mask-coverage target.
Add edited-distractor exclusion loss, then sweep loss weights on CompoEdit-1 held-outs for ≥90% region recall and ≤5% distractor coverage.
Train CompoEdit-1 mask variants at exclusion-loss weights 0.1, 0.3, and 1.0; score held-out region recall and distractor coverage.
CompoEdit-1 exclusion-sweep report contains three mask checkpoints, held-out region-recall and distractor-coverage tables, and evaluation scripts.
Reproduce all three checkpoints’ CompoEdit-1 scores from the sweep report and verify ≥90% region recall with ≤5% distractor coverage.
Reproduced CompoEdit-1 scores: exclusion weight 0.3 retained 91% relation-region recall and reduced edited-distractor coverage from 13% to 4%.
Under simultaneous two-distractor edits on unseen combinations, 0.3-weight exclusion masks maintain ≥90% relation-region recall and ≤5% distractor coverage.
Using the exclusion-sweep report’s 0.3-weight checkpoint, measure region recall and distractor coverage on held-out simultaneous two-distractor edits.
On CompoEdit-1 unseen combinations with simultaneous two-distractor edits, 0.3-weight masks achieved 90.5% relation-region recall and 4.8% distractor coverage.
Select 0.3-weight masks for end-to-end VQA evaluation; both single- and two-distractor tests meet recall and coverage thresholds.
CompoEdit-1 two-distractor evaluation bundle contains held-out edit pairs, region annotations, mask predictions, and per-combination recall and coverage scores.
Train a typed scene-graph VQA model with intervention-specific graph updates and answer supervision on changed versus unchanged causal subgraphs.
Annotate CompoEdit-1 intervention graphs, train graph VQA, and test ≥80% paired accuracy and ≤5% distractor flips on unseen combinations.
Use the exclusion-sweep report’s 0.3-weight mask checkpoint to propose graph nodes; annotate intervention-affected edges in 2,000 CompoEdit-1 pairs.
CompoEdit-1 InterventionGraph-v1 contains 2,000 paired images with mask-derived nodes, typed relations, and annotated intervention-affected edges.
Can InterventionGraph-v1 distinguish answer-changing relation edits from irrelevant attribute edits on unseen object–attribute combinations?
On CompoEdit-1 unseen combinations, intervention-affected graph edges identify answer-changing edits with ≥90% F1 and irrelevant edits with ≥95% specificity.
Audit InterventionGraph-v1 affected-edge labels against blinded causal-edit judgments on held-out combinations; calculate answer-changing F1 and irrelevant-edit specificity.
Blinded CompoEdit-1 audit found 86% answer-changing F1 and 96% irrelevant-edit specificity, missing the 90% F1 target.
Defer graph VQA training until affected-edge recall improves; 86% answer-changing F1 risks suppressing valid counterfactual answer changes.
Benchmark mask-grounded VQA against frozen InterventionGraph-v1 update rules using the two-distractor bundle; measure paired accuracy and distractor flips.
On unseen CompoEdit-1 two-distractor pairs, frozen graph rules reached 82% paired accuracy, 4% distractor flips; mask-grounded VQA reached 76%, 7%.
Repair InterventionGraph-v1’s missed affected edges; require ≥90% affected-edge recall before training graph VQA and testing paired accuracy and distractor flips.
After affected-edge recall reached 92%, trained graph VQA scored 78% paired accuracy and 6% distractor flips on unseen CompoEdit-1 combinations.
After lifting the label-based training deferral, retain frozen graph rules provisionally; trained VQA misses both targets.
Gate mask-grounded VQA answer updates with frozen graph rules, allowing changes only when question-relevant edges are altered.
Can graph-gated mask VQA suppress irrelevant-edit flips without blocking answers to changed question-relevant relations on unseen combinations?
Despite imperfect affected-edge labels, frozen graph gating of 0.3-weight mask VQA achieves ≥80% paired accuracy and ≤5% distractor flips.
Gate 0.3-weight mask VQA with frozen InterventionGraph-v1 rules; score paired accuracy and irrelevant-edit flips on unseen CompoEdit-1 pairs.
Graph-gated mask VQA scored 79% paired accuracy and 3% irrelevant-edit flips on unseen CompoEdit-1, missing the accuracy target.
A 0.9 mask-VQA causal-edit-confidence override of frozen graph gates achieves ≥80% paired accuracy and ≤5% distractor flips on unseen combinations.
Apply 0.9-confidence mask-VQA overrides to InterventionGraph-v1 gates; measure fixed-question paired accuracy and distractor flips on unseen CompoEdit-1 combinations.
GateOverride-0.9 evaluation package contains confidence-gated predictions, fixed-question pair labels, distractor-edit flags, and reproducible scoring scripts.
GateOverride-0.9 achieved 81% fixed-question paired accuracy and 4% irrelevant-edit flips on unseen CompoEdit-1 combinations.
Recompute GateOverride-0.9 paired accuracy and irrelevant-edit flips from n39’s evaluation package, auditing unseen-combination strata against 80% and 5% targets.
Independently rerun GateOverride-0.9 package scripts; verify prediction–label alignment and report paired accuracy and irrelevant-edit flips by unseen-combination stratum.
Independent audit found mismatched edit IDs in GateOverride-0.9; corrected scores were 77% paired accuracy and 6% irrelevant-edit flips.
Suspend graph-gated mask VQA; corrected 77% paired accuracy and 6% flips overturn the reported 81% and 4%, missing both targets.
Train pairwise edit-difference VQA with answer-change supervision and distractor-invariance loss on audited image IDs, without graph gates.
Following graph-gate suspension, reconcile edit IDs, train pairwise VQA, and test ≥80% paired accuracy and ≤5% distractor flips.
Reconcile GateOverride-0.9 edit IDs against image hashes and pair labels; export collision-free CompoEdit-1 train and held-out manifests.
GateOverride-0.9-v2 replaces mismatched edit IDs with hash-verified, collision-free manifests and aligned pair labels, distractor flags, and scoring scripts.
Validate GateOverride-0.9-v2 hash-to-label alignment, then train pairwise edit-difference VQA and score held-out paired accuracy and distractor flips.
With hash-verified labels, pairwise edit-difference VQA scored 82% paired accuracy but 8% distractor flips on unseen combinations.
Can stronger distractor-invariance training reduce pairwise VQA’s 8% distractor flips below 5% without sacrificing 82% paired accuracy?
Adding question-matched distractor edits at a 2:1 training ratio reduces flips to ≤5% while preserving ≥80% paired accuracy.
Using hash-verified manifests, retrain pairwise VQA with 2:1 question-matched distractor edits; compare held-out paired accuracy and flips against 82%/8%.
At 2:1 distractor training, pairwise VQA achieved 81% paired accuracy and 4.5% flips on hash-verified unseen CompoEdit-1 combinations.
Freeze the 2:1 pairwise VQA checkpoint; independently audit hash-aligned fixed-question pairs and distractor edits against both acceptance thresholds.
Independently rescore 2:1 and baseline VQA checkpoints on hash-verified CompoEdit-1; inspect pair alignment and calculate paired accuracy and flip rates.
GateOverride-0.9-v3 revises v2’s scoring scripts and adds independently rescored 2:1/baseline predictions, checkpoint hashes, and pair-alignment checks.
Audit GateOverride-0.9-v3 hashes and pair alignment; recompute 2:1 pairwise VQA accuracy and distractor flips on unseen combinations.
GateOverride-0.9-v3 audit verified hash alignment; 2:1 pairwise VQA retained 81% fixed-question paired accuracy and 4.5% irrelevant-edit flips.
Adopt audited 2:1 pairwise VQA: 81% paired accuracy and 4.5% distractor flips meet targets; baseline flips were 8%.
